skill.name: scientific-brainstorming
skill.description: A research ideation partner for generating hypotheses, exploring interdisciplinary links, challenging assumptions, and planning scientific next steps.
skill.summary: Guide structured scientific brainstorming from research context to promising ideas and next steps.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives from normal brainstorming prose, not system reconnaissance behavior. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe tool behavior was found in the reviewed skill files.

static_findings.snippet: - What if you did less but better?
- Methods are tools, not rigid procedures—adapt as needed
- Avoid jargon from fields outside the scientist's expertise unless explaining it clearly.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line asks whether a research approach can be simplified. It is brainstorming guidance and does not request host, network, account, or environment reconnaissance.
The line says brainstorming methods should be adapted as needed. It refers to ideation techniques, not system tools, file discovery, or infrastructure probing.
The line advises clear explanations when using unfamiliar scientific jargon. It contains no instruction to inspect systems, enumerate resources, or gather operational details.

content.value_statement: Scientists need fresh hypotheses and practical study directions when research becomes narrow. This skill guides structured scientific brainstorming with analogies, assumption checks, methods, and next steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides research conversations through context, idea generation, evaluation, and synthesis.
Generates hypotheses, research questions, experimental directions, and study plan options.
Applies SCAMPER, Six Thinking Hats, morphological analysis, TRIZ, and biomimicry methods.
Challenges assumptions and proposes analogies from other scientific fields.
Suggests pilot experiments, literature search angles, collaborators, and immediate next steps.
Helps reframe stalled or overly conservative research discussions.
limitations: Does not validate scientific truth or replace peer review.
Requires clear domain context, constraints, and research goals from the user.
Does not run experiments, analyze datasets, or access private literature.
Generated ideas may need ethics, safety, regulatory, or feasibility review.

use_cases.title: Find New Research Directions
use_cases.description: Explore fresh hypotheses, neglected variables, and research gaps for a current project.

use_cases.title: Design Better Experiments
use_cases.description: Turn early ideas into testable studies, pilot experiments, and practical next steps.

use_cases.title: Explore Cross-Field Methods
use_cases.description: Borrow useful concepts from other disciplines to approach a difficult research problem.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Research Brainstorm
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for an open ideation session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me brainstorm new directions for my research. My field is [field], my topic is [topic], and my main challenge is [challenge].

prompt_templates.title: Challenge My Assumptions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for reframing a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this research idea and identify assumptions I may be making. Then suggest alternative frames and testable hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Build Experimental Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate several experimental approaches for testing [hypothesis]. Include low-resource pilots, stronger validation studies, and likely obstacles.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Interdisciplinary Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for complex research planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cross-domain analogies and structured brainstorming methods to develop a research strategy for [problem]. Include methods, collaborators, risks, and next steps.

output_examples.input: I study antibiotic resistance and need new angles for biofilm disruption.
output: Hypotheses involving nutrient gradients, mechanical stress, and quorum sensing interference.
Analogies from ecosystem succession and urban network resilience.
Pilot experiments using controlled surface chemistry and time-lapse imaging.

output_examples.input: My neuroscience project feels too incremental.
output: Reframed questions at molecular, circuit, behavioral, and population scales.
Assumptions to test, including measurement bias and model organism limits.
Three bolder study directions with feasibility notes and first experiments.

output_examples.input: I want to apply biomimicry to sustainable materials research.
output: Natural models such as nacre, spider silk, lotus leaves, and bone remodeling.
Abstracted design principles for strength, self-repair, adhesion, and water control.
Candidate experiments comparing material structure, fabrication method, and durability.

best_practices: Share the research field, current model, constraints, and what has already failed.
Ask for both bold ideas and practical first experiments.
Review generated ideas with domain experts before acting on them.
anti_patterns: Do not treat brainstorming output as validated scientific evidence.
Do not hide safety, ethics, budget, or data constraints from the session.
Do not stop at many ideas without selecting next steps.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps generate research ideas, hypotheses, experimental options, and interdisciplinary connections through structured scientific brainstorming.

faq.question: Can it replace a literature review?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest search angles and gaps, but users must verify ideas against current literature.

faq.question: Does it work outside laboratory science?
faq.answer: Yes. It can support social science, engineering, clinical research, design research, and other evidence-based fields.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your field, question, current assumptions, constraints, available methods, and what kind of output you want.

faq.question: Can it design complete studies?
faq.answer: It can outline study options and next steps, but experts must check feasibility, ethics, safety, and statistics.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex.
